lines.japanese: それから太陽が何度も沈んで、早や２年と半年。
lines.english: Since then, the sun has set and set again, and already two and a half years have passed.

lines.japanese: ひととき湧いたあの甘い期待もいまは昔。
lines.english: That brief flowering of sweet expectation belongs to the distant past.

lines.japanese: 僕は形ばかりの受験生になって、迎えるかどうかも分からない受験日を前に、参考書をめくったりめくらなかったりして無為な日々を過ごしている。
lines.english: Now I am a college applicant in name alone. With no certainty that I will even be here for the entrance exams, I pass my idle days sometimes turning the pages of a study guide, sometimes not.

lines.japanese: 森里君とは進路が違ったので、同じクラスになれたのは最初の一年だけだった。
lines.english: Morisato and I chose different academic tracks, so our first year was the only one we spent in the same class.

lines.japanese: つまり、僕に友達がいたのは初めの一年だけだったことになる。
lines.english: Which is to say, it was also the only year in which I had a friend.

lines.japanese: でも、それまで友達のいなかった僕は、その一年間で森里君からいろんなことを学んだ。
lines.english: But I’d never had a friend before, and Morisato taught me all kinds of things that year.

lines.japanese: 大きな声でげらげらと笑われるのは恥ずかしかったけど、だけど彼がそうしてくれることで、僕は世間の目を気にするということを少しずつ学んでいった。
lines.english: It embarrassed me when he laughed so loudly, but by doing that, little by little, he taught me to care how the world saw me.

lines.japanese: だから僕はこの世界でひどく消極的な人間になってしまったけど、そのぶん白眼視されることも少なくなったから、彼にはとても感謝しているんだ。
lines.english: That’s why I ended up so withdrawn in this world. But it also meant fewer people gave me dirty looks, so I’m really grateful to him.

lines.japanese: そういえばちょっと前に、僕がロビーでぼんやりしていたら森里君が声をかけてくれた。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Morisato talked to me not long ago when I was spacing out in the lobby.

lines.japanese: 彼は一緒にいた新しい友人たちに、僕を紹介してくれた。
lines.english: He introduced me to the new friends he was with.

lines.japanese: 「これが羽田。ほら、このまえケータ君には話したじゃん、あの、ブルガリの」
lines.english: “This is Haneda. C’mon, Keita, I told you about him before. The Bulgari guy.”

lines.japanese: 僕の知らない彼のクラスメイトたちは、ああ、と言って面白そうに笑っていた。それを見て森里君もほっとしたみたいに笑う。
lines.english: His classmates, none of whom I knew, went, “Oh,” and smiled like they found it funny. Seeing that, Morisato smiled too, like he was relieved.

lines.japanese: それから僕は、久しぶりにプロレス技の練習相手になった。どうやら森里君の最近のお気に入りは、シャイニングウィザードみたいだった。
lines.english: Then, for the first time in ages, I served as his practice dummy for professional wrestling moves. Morisato’s latest favorite appeared to be the Shining Wizard.

lines.japanese: 森里君は加減してくれたけど、彼の友人たちはわりと容赦なかった。でも、軍用ワイバーンの空気を震わせる尻尾の一撃に比べればぜんぜん大したことのない膝蹴りだったから、僕は笑顔を崩すこともなかった。
lines.english: Morisato held back, though his friends were rather less merciful. Still, their knee strikes were nothing beside the air-shaking lash of a military wyvern's tail, and my smile never faltered.

lines.japanese: 「つえー、羽田つえー！　ナイスサンドバッグ！　かかか、ねっ、すごいでしょコレ羽田って！」
lines.english: “He’s tough! Haneda’s a beast! Best punching bag ever! Ka-ka-ka! See? Didn’t I tell you this Haneda guy was amazing?”

lines.japanese: 森里君は僕の肩を掴んで腹筋にこぶしを押しつけてきた。昔と同じ肩までのロングヘアだったけど、ピアスと香水はあの頃と変わっていた。
lines.english: Morisato gripped my shoulder and pressed his fist against my stomach. His hair still fell to his shoulders as it had back then, though both his earrings and his perfume had changed.

lines.japanese: もう積算いくらかも忘れたブルガリの立て替え代は、そういえばまだ払ってもらっていない。
lines.english: Now that I thought of it, he had yet to repay me for any of the Bulgari I had bought him. I had long since lost track of the total.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そーいえばおまえ、渡来といつ別れたの」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. When did you and Watarai break up?”

lines.japanese: 「え、別れてないよ……」
lines.english: “We haven’t…”

lines.japanese: 「うっそでー。ぜんぜん一緒にいねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Bullshit. You’re never even together.”

lines.japanese: 「いや……だから前に言ったじゃん。おれ、みんなの前でそういうの、格好悪くて嫌だから……」
lines.english: “No… I told you before. Acting like that in front of everyone is lame. I hate it…”

lines.japanese: 「ぷぷっ！　んな、ド高め相手に余裕ぶっこける立場じゃねーだろおまえ。ねータムラ君、明日香さまがオトコと歩いてんの見たんだよねー」
lines.english: “Pfft! You bagged somebody that far out of your league; you’re in no position to play it cool. Right, Tamura? You saw Lady Asuka walking around with some guy.”

lines.japanese: 森里君は昔みたいに、僕の首をがっちりロックして締めつける。彼の脇腹あたりで固定されていた僕の視界は、森里君の友人が頷いたのかどうかを捕えられなかった。
lines.english: Just like old times, Morisato locked an arm tight around my neck and squeezed. All I could see was somewhere around his ribs, so I couldn’t tell whether his friend nodded.

lines.japanese: だけど、どのみちその真偽は僕にとってなんら意味を為さない。
lines.english: But whether it was true or false meant nothing to me in either case.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが誰と親密になろうが、僕には関係のないことだ。僕と彼女の交わした盟約は、一般的な意味での恋人関係には程遠いものだったから。
lines.english: Whoever Watarai might grow close to was no concern of mine. The covenant between us was far removed from what people ordinarily meant by a romantic relationship.

lines.japanese: 美空学園で最初の春──あの森里君たちのいたずらのあと、渡来さんのセンセーショナルな交際宣言はその日のうちに広く学園中を駆けめぐっていた。
lines.english: That first spring at Misora Academy—after Morisato and the others played their prank, Watarai’s sensational declaration that we were a couple raced through the entire school before the day was out.

lines.japanese: そして放課後、いやぁびっくりする冗談だったなぁと喫驚冷めやらぬ僕の前に、彼女がひょいと鞄を提げてやってきて、みんなの見ている前で堂々と「帰ろ」と言った。
lines.english: Then, after school, while I was still marveling at what an astonishing joke it had been, she appeared before me with her bag dangling from one hand and said, bold as could be in front of everyone, “Let’s go home.”

lines.japanese: 背筋を伸ばして早足で廊下を進むその後ろ姿に、僕は数歩の距離を置いて付いていった。制服の短いスカートから覗く黒いストッキングの脚線美がひどく綺麗だったことを、いまでも鮮明に覚えている。
lines.english: I followed several paces behind as she strode briskly down the hall, back straight. Even now, I remember with perfect clarity how beautiful her legs looked in black stockings beneath the short skirt of her uniform.
“Well?”

lines.japanese: なにか喋ろうと口を開く決心が付いたころ、彼女が体ごとくるりと振りかえった。颯爽とひるがえる長い髪が、海外ドラマの女エージェントみたいで格好よかった。
lines.english: Just as I had finally resolved to open my mouth and say something, she wheeled around, long hair flying with such dash that she looked like a female agent in a foreign television drama.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君。だよね？　渡来ですよろしく」
lines.english: “Haneda. Right? I’m Watarai. Nice to meet you.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　ああ、はい、こちらこそ……」
lines.english: “What? Oh—yes. Nice to meet you too…”

lines.japanese: 「で。付きあってくれって言ってたけど、私どこに付きあえばいいの？」
lines.english: “So. You said you wanted me to go out with you. Where am I going with you?”

lines.japanese: 「え……あれ？　いや……」
lines.english: “What…? Wait. No…”

lines.japanese: 「ごはん？　買い物？　産婦人科？」
lines.english: “Dinner? Shopping? The OB-GYN?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはお嬢さま然とした声や外見のわりに、さばさばと歯切れよく話すひとだった。
lines.english: Watarai looked and sounded like a proper young lady, but she spoke briskly and straight to the point.

lines.japanese: 森里君以外の同級生に無関心だった僕は、そのとき二重の意味で戸惑った──彼女の超然としたそんな物腰と、「付きあう」という言葉の捉えちがいと。
lines.english: Having taken no interest in any classmate but Morisato, I found myself doubly bewildered: by her cool, detached manner, and by her curious interpretation of the words ‘go out.’

lines.japanese: 「ええと……ごめん、あれ違うんだ。あれは森里君たちが勝手に言ってただけで、おれはべつに……」
lines.english: “Um… I’m sorry, but that wasn’t true. Morisato and the others said it on their own. I didn’t actually…”

lines.japanese: 「うん。だろうね。じゃあ、私に用はない？」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. I thought so. Then you don’t need anything from me?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　う、うん……」
lines.english: “What? N-no…”

lines.japanese: 「そ。それじゃ。ばいばい」
lines.english: “Okay. See you. Bye-bye.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは立てた五本の指をほんのわずか左右に揺らして、美空学園の正門アーチをくぐり抜けていった。
lines.english: Watarai raised all five fingers and gave them the slightest sway from side to side, then passed beneath the arch of Misora Academy’s front gate.

lines.japanese: 僕は釣られて、つい同じぐらいの振り幅で手を振りかえしたけれど、一瞬のち、そのまま無言で見送ってる場合じゃないと気付いた。
lines.english: Without thinking, I returned her little wave with one just as small. A moment later, I realized this was no time to stand there silently watching her leave.

lines.japanese: 「え？　あれ？　ちょっと待って」
lines.english: “What? Wait. Hold on.”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 彼女はすぐに笑顔で振りかえったけど、僕が呼びとめた理由にはあまり興味なさそうな表情だった。世の中には瞬きするより早く笑顔を作れるひとがいる。たぶん彼女もそういう人種なんだろう。
lines.english: She turned back at once with a smile, though her face showed little interest in why I had stopped her. Some people can make a smile faster than they can blink. She was probably one of them.

lines.japanese: 「えと……いや、おれが言うのもなんだけど、どうしよう、みんな誤解してると思うよ」
lines.english: “Um… no, I mean, maybe it’s not my place to say, but… what do we do? I think everyone’s got the wrong idea.”

lines.japanese: 「あー。かもね」
lines.english: “Oh. They might.”

lines.japanese: 無関心な笑顔のまま、渡来さんは短く答えた。あまりに落ちついているから、僕は彼女が事情を呑みこめていないものかと思った。
lines.english: Watarai answered briefly, her smile still unconcerned. She was so composed that I began to wonder if she had failed to understand the situation.

lines.japanese: 「ええと……だから、みんなの言う『付き合う』ってのは買い物に付き合うとかそういうことじゃなくて、つまり、おれと渡来さんが、その……」
lines.english: “Um… See, when everyone said ‘go out,’ they didn’t mean going shopping together or anything like that. They meant that you and I were… you know…”

lines.japanese: 「彼氏彼女のお付きあい」
lines.english: “Going out as boyfriend and girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そう。それ」
lines.english: “Yes. That.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは通学鞄を持っていない方の手を首の高さに掲げて、親指と小指をぴこぴこ立てたり折ったりしていた。保母さんみたいに可愛らしい身振りと、社長秘書みたいに毅然とした姿勢がまるでちぐはぐだ。
lines.english: Watarai raised her free hand to her neck and flexed her thumb and little finger up and down. The nursery-school sweetness of the gesture clashed strangely with her executive secretary’s bearing.

lines.japanese: 「……え、分かってるの？」
lines.english: “…You understood?”

lines.japanese: 「え、あの流れで分からないほどお馬鹿ちゃんに見えるの私？」
lines.english: “Do I look silly enough not to understand after all that?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は視線を首ごと斜め下に傾けて不服を漏らした。
lines.english: She tilted her head, looking down to one side as she voiced her displeasure.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうじゃなくてさ。じゃあ、なんで分かっててあんな──」
lines.english: “No, that’s not what I meant. But then, if you knew, why did you—”

lines.japanese: 「可哀想だったから」
lines.english: “Because I felt sorry for you.”

lines.japanese: 頭を正面に戻して、彼女ははっきり答えた。億劫そうな張りのない声で、僕はすこし怯んだ。
lines.english: She faced forward again and answered plainly. Her voice was languid and flat, and it made me shrink a little.

lines.japanese: 「え……なにが？」
lines.english: “For… what?”

lines.japanese: 「あと、いじめの片棒担がされるの嫌だったし」
lines.english: “And I didn’t want to help them bully you.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　何それ、やだな、そんなんじゃないよ。森里君はおれの友達なんだ。ちょっとした冗談だよ、みんなが楽しんでくれたから、おれはそれでいいんだ」
lines.english: “What? No, that sounds awful. It wasn’t like that. Morisato is my friend. It was just a little joke, and everyone enjoyed it. That’s enough for me.”

lines.japanese: 「ふうん──」
lines.english: “I see—”

lines.japanese: 子供の無邪気な嘘に合わせる慈母のような笑顔。弥勒菩薩を思わせるアルカイックスマイル。嘘つくみたいな甘い声で彼女は言った。
lines.english: She smiled as a loving mother might at a child’s innocent lie: the archaic smile of a statue of the bodhisattva Maitreya. Then, in a voice so sweet it sounded like a lie, she said:

lines.japanese: 「──だったら余計なことしちゃったね。ごめん」
lines.english: “—then I guess I shouldn’t have gotten involved. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、いいけど」
lines.english: “Ha ha. That’s all right.”

lines.japanese: 「え、いや、よくないよ。だって、その、付きあうってこと、誤解されたままだし……もし他のクラスとかにまで広まってたら……」
lines.english: “No, wait, that’s not okay. I mean, um, they still think we’re dating… What if it’s spread to the other classes too…?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか。迷惑だよね。羽田君には羽田君の好きな子がいるんだもんね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. That would be a problem. You already have a girl you like, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「え……いや、おれの方じゃなくて、そっちが……渡来さんの方が迷惑でしょ」
lines.english: “What…? No, I don’t mean for me. I mean you. It would cause trouble for you, wouldn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに」
lines.english: “Not really.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は言葉通り「べつに」という涼しい顔をしていた。僕の方は……たぶん間抜けな顔をしていたと思う。
lines.english: Her cool expression said exactly what her words did: not really. I, on the other hand, probably looked rather stupid.

lines.japanese: 「んー、迷惑どころか、そう思われてるとかえって助かるかも。帰り待ち伏せしてる先輩とかいて鬱陶しかったし」
lines.english: “Actually, it might help if people think that. There are upperclassmen who wait to ambush me after school. It’s annoying.”

lines.japanese: 眉をひそめ、首の後ろをさすりながら彼女は言う。なんだか仏様がいきなり僕らの立っているところに下りてきたみたいで、ちょっと驚いたけれど少し気が楽になった。
lines.english: She frowned and rubbed the back of her neck. It was as though a buddha had suddenly descended to the ground where we stood. The surprise of it left me oddly more at ease.

lines.japanese: 「私、基本的に人間嫌いだから誰とも付きあうつもりないんだけど、ほら、断りつづけてると、無駄に恨まれたり僻まれたりするでしょ。お高くとまってるように見られたりとか」
lines.english: “I basically hate people, so I don’t plan to date anyone. But when you keep turning them down, some hold a pointless grudge or get jealous. They decide you think you’re too good for them.”

lines.japanese: 「なにかと出る杭は打たれるのが共同生活──あ、いま私、痛いこと言ってるね。うん、失言。編集で切っといて」
lines.english: “Any nail that sticks out gets hammered down—that’s communal living for you. Oh, that sounded painfully pretentious. Yeah. Bad line. Cut it in editing.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “R-right.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は鞄を持ってない方の手で、二本指をちょきちょきさせる。思ったよりテンポの速いひとだ。僕はすこし遅れて愛想笑いを返した。
lines.english: With her free hand, she snipped two fingers like scissors. She moved at a quicker tempo than I had expected. A beat late, I answered with a polite laugh.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あはは、もてるひとも大変なんだ」
lines.english: “Ah, ha ha… I guess being popular isn’t easy either.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。たとえば、そういうことを言われたときのリアクションに困るよね」
lines.english: “Yeah. Like, when someone says something like that, you don’t know how you’re supposed to react.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうか、はは……」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. Ha ha…”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、引かれるし」
lines.english: “See? Now you’re put off.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことは」
lines.english: “N-no, I’m not.”

lines.japanese: 「でもさ、下手に謙遜しても嘘つけとか、ぶってるとか思われるし、ほんと困るんだよね。そもそも、こんな解説しちゃうパターンがいちばん最悪なんだと思うけど。あははっ、ごめんね」
lines.english: “But if I try to be modest, people say I’m lying, or putting on an act. It’s a real problem. Though I suppose the worst possible response is explaining all of this out loud. Ah-ha-ha. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、いいけど……」
lines.english: “No, it’s all right…”

lines.japanese: 「実際ずーっとそういう目に遭ってきたせいで、すっかり世間ずれしちゃったんだよねー」
lines.english: “It’s been happening to me forever, so I’m totally jaded now, you know?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはまたこうべを垂れて、アスファルトの舗装に溜息のような声を落とした。もしかしたら、右斜め下４５度に向けて不満や困惑の呟きを吹きかけるのが、彼女の小さな癖なのかもしれない。
lines.english: Watarai bowed her head again and let a sigh-like voice fall onto the asphalt. Perhaps it was a small habit of hers, breathing her complaints and perplexities into a point forty-five degrees down and to the right.

lines.japanese: 「そんな面倒に巻きこまれるぐらいなら、私むしろ誰とも絡まないでいいかなー、ひとりのが楽かなー、友達もいらないかなー、とかって風にも思うんだけど──」
lines.english: “If dealing with people means getting dragged into all that trouble, sometimes I think I’d rather have nothing to do with anyone. Being alone is easier. Maybe I don’t need friends either—”

lines.japanese: 「──かと言って敵に回しちゃうとさ、それはそれで困るんだ。こんな、悟った風なこと言っちゃってるけど、私ほんとは全然。羽田君みたいに打たれづよくないから」
lines.english: “—but making enemies causes its own problems. I know I’m talking as if I’ve risen above it all, but I really haven’t. I’m not as hard to hurt as you are, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「おれ？　え、おれ、打たれづよいの？」
lines.english: “Me? Am I hard to hurt?”

lines.japanese: 「づよいでしょ？　じゃなかったら、なんらかの感情が病的に欠落してるか。どっちかだと思うな」
lines.english: “Aren't you? Either that, or some emotion is pathologically absent from you. I think it has to be one of the two.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ごめん、悪い意味で言ってるんじゃなくて。尊敬する。ほんとほんと、すごいなーって。なんでそんなに心が広いんだろーって。だから実は、こないだからちょっと注目してたんだ。あ」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry, I don’t mean that in a bad way. I respect you. Really, really. I kept thinking, wow, you’re amazing. How can anyone be that big-hearted? So, actually, I’ve kinda had my eye on you lately. Oh.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は突然ドキッとするようなことを言った、と思ったらすぐに眉をひそめて横を向いた。
lines.english: The moment the startling words left her mouth, her brow knit and she turned aside.

lines.japanese: 「いまの発言は迂闊だー」
lines.english: “That was caaareless of me.”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　なに？」
lines.english: “Huh? What was?”

lines.japanese: 「前の学校でね」
lines.english: “At my old school—”

lines.japanese: そして向きなおって続けた。
lines.english: She turned back to me and continued.

lines.japanese: 「入学してすぐ私、おまえは痴女かってほど短いスカート穿いてる先輩たちに呼びだされて。その中の、こーいうーソウルフルな頭をしたおねーさんに──」
lines.english: “Right after I enrolled, a group of upperclassmen in skirts so short you’d think they were exhibitionists summoned me. One of them had this wonderfully soulful, corkscrew-permed hair—”

lines.japanese: 細い人差し指が、長い髪に沿って、いくつも小さな円を作りながら滑りおちていった。
lines.english: Her slender forefinger traveled down the length of her hair, describing a succession of tiny circles.

lines.japanese: 「──おまえみたいな女はむやみに男を誉めるなって怒られた。『テメ媚びてんじゃネーヨ！』だって。あ、いまの結構似てた」
lines.english: “—and she told me a girl like me shouldn’t go around complimenting guys. ‘Don’t you fuckin’ flirt!’ she said. Oh, that was actually a pretty good impression.”

lines.japanese: 「ひどいよね。言論封殺。人種差別だっての。そんな性格だからフラれるんであって、私があんたの彼氏に思わせぶりなことを言ったとか言ってないとかは、関・係・ないっ。なんちゃって」
lines.english: “Terrible, isn’t it? Censorship. Racial discrimination, even. Your rotten personality is why he dumped you; whether I did or did not lead your boyfriend on has ab-so-lute-ly nothing to do with it. Just kidding.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、引いてる？」
lines.english: “Oh. Have I put you off?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、あ、いや、引いてない、よ？」
lines.english: “What? No, no. You haven’t. Really.”

lines.japanese: 「待って。補足説明させて。あのね、それまでに私は、その先輩という人物から度重なるパワーハラスメントを受けててね。そりゃあもう、人権や尊厳を大いに傷付けられてきたわけ」
lines.english: “Wait. Let me provide some context. You see, by that point this upperclassman had already subjected me to repeated abuses of power. My human rights and personal dignity had suffered terribly.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう有形無形の嫌がらせを、いくつも、いくつも、いくつも耐えしのんできた、う・え・で・のっ！　ハイさっきの可愛らしい皮肉。ね。健全な反応でしょ？」
lines.english: “After putting up with all that harassment—again, and again, and again—only THEN! came that cute little jab from before. See? Totally healthy reaction, right?”
“Y-yes…”

lines.japanese: 僕は顎を引くように頷いた。淀みなく流れる彼女の声には、雪融けの渓流みたいな速さと厳しさと美しさがあった。
lines.english: I nodded by tucking in my chin. Her voice poured forth without pause, possessing the speed, severity, and beauty of a mountain stream in the spring thaw.

lines.japanese: 「で、話戻るんだけど」
lines.english: “Anyway, back to what we were talking about.”
“Right…”

lines.japanese: その滑らかなせせらぎに打たれるまま、適当な相槌を打った。
lines.english: Buffeted by that fluent current, I offered a vague murmur of assent.

lines.japanese: 「私としては説明するのも面倒だし、べつに誤解されたままでも構わないんだけど、羽田君は困るよね」
lines.english: “Me, I can’t be bothered to explain it, and I don’t really care if they keep getting it wrong. But it’s a problem for you, right?”

lines.japanese: 「はっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: たしかに前置きはあったけど、本当にくるっと話が戻ってきてちょっと狼狽した。
lines.english: She had warned me we were going back to it, but when she really did snap right back to the subject, I panicked a little.

lines.japanese: 「あ、どう、かな……いや、べつに、困らないとは思うけど……」
lines.english: “Oh. I’m not… sure. No, I don’t think it would really cause me any trouble…”

lines.japanese: 「ほんと？　助かる！　それじゃ、しばらくこのままでもいいかなあ」
lines.english: “Really? That’d be a huge help! Then maybe we can leave things like this for a while?”

lines.japanese: このとき彼女の見せた申しわけなさそうな笑顔が、僕の初恋の原子核になっているんだと思う。
lines.english: I think the apologetic smile she gave me then became the nucleus of my first love.

lines.japanese: 友人の言葉を借りるなら、一個の適当なとっかかり。好きの理由は後から後から付いてくる。
lines.english: To borrow my friend's words, it was one random little hook. The reasons for loving her came later, one after another.

lines.japanese: 本当だったよ、森里君。
lines.english: You were right, Morisato.

lines.japanese: 「そもそもさ、つーかコレ何度も聞いてっけどさ、おまえら本当は付きあってなかったんだろ？」
lines.english: “I mean, I’ve asked you this a million times, but you two were never really going out, were you?”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんで過去形なの」
lines.english: “Why are you putting it in the past tense?”

lines.japanese: 「羽田ァ、俺にだけ本当のこと言えって、な？」
lines.english: “Haneda. C’mon, you can tell me the truth. Just me, okay?”

lines.japanese: たったひとりの友人にそんなことを言われて、僕はちょっと揺らいだ。でも渡来さんに無断で、勝手なことはできない。
lines.english: When my one and only friend put it that way, my resolve wavered a little. But I could not act on my own without Watarai’s permission.

lines.japanese: 「……じゃあ、向こうに聞いてみてよ」
lines.english: “…Then ask her.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、いんだけどさ。そんな言うならおまえ、やったら教えろよ、へへ。じゃな」
lines.english: “Fine by me. If you’re gonna insist, though, tell me when you finally do it. Heh heh. See ya.”

lines.japanese: 森里君は、ピッチャーマウンドでプロ野球の監督がへこたれた投手にするみたいに、僕のお尻を力いっぱい叩いていった。
lines.english: Morisato slapped me hard on the backside, like a professional baseball manager visiting the mound to rally his flagging pitcher.

lines.japanese: 「って、うぉおい！　ちょ、待てって田村君！　だから、なんでいつも先行っちゃうんだよォ！」
lines.english: “Whoa, hey! Wait up, Tamura! Why do you always take off without me?”

lines.japanese: 二年前はだいたいグループの先頭を歩いていた森里君が、僕の知らない友人たちの背中を追ってシンデレラ階段を駆けのぼっていった。
lines.english: Two years ago, Morisato had usually walked at the head of the group. Now he ran up the Cinderella Staircase after friends I did not know.

lines.japanese: その後ろ姿を見送りながら、僕はエントランスロビーのベンチにゆっくり腰を下ろした。
lines.english: I watched his retreating back, then slowly lowered myself onto a bench in the entrance lobby.

lines.japanese: 彼に嘘はついていない。あれから二年半が経ったけど、お互いとくに関係を解消する申し出がなかったから──
lines.english: I had not lied to him. Two and a half years had passed, but neither of us had ever proposed dissolving our relationship—

lines.japanese: ──だからいまだに渡来さんは、僕の「彼女」ということになってるみたいだ。
lines.english: —and so, apparently, Watarai remains my ‘girlfriend’ to this day.

lines.japanese: すでに信じてるひとなんていないだろうし、僕自身まるで他人事としか思えないけれど。
lines.english: I doubt anyone believes it anymore, and even to me, it feels like it has nothing to do with me.

lines.japanese: 幸か不幸か、僕と渡来さんは一年・二年・三年とずっと同じクラスだった。
lines.english: For better or worse, Watarai and I were classmates in our first year, our second, and now our third.

lines.japanese: 彼女は今日もその人間嫌いな本性を器用に隠して、クラスの仲間と積極的に消極的な関係を築いている。僕と会話したことはと言えば、この二年半の学園生活で数えるほどだって言うのに。
lines.english: Even today, she skillfully conceals her true distaste for humanity and actively maintains a passive relationship with the rest of the class. Yet in two and a half years at this school, the conversations she has had with me could be counted on one hand.

lines.japanese: この世界から消えゆく日を指折り数えながら、ときおり僕はそのあまり多くはない会話の断片を思いだす。
lines.english: As I count down the days until I vanish from this world, now and then I remember fragments of those few conversations.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、まだ好きな子できないの？」
lines.english: “Haneda, still haven’t found a girl you like?”

lines.japanese: いつか彼女は言った。
lines.english: She asked me that once.

lines.japanese: 「まさか、私に遠慮とかしてないよね？　青春時代に恋しとかないと老後に後悔すると思うよ」
lines.english: “You aren’t holding back on my account, are you? If you don’t fall in love while you’re young, I think you’ll regret it in your old age.”

lines.japanese: 「私はいつでも景気よくフラれてあげるからね。そのときが来たら、たぶん……ちょっと寂しいと思うけど」
lines.english: “Whenever you’re ready, I’ll cheerfully let you dump me. When that day comes, I’ll probably… be a little lonely.”

lines.japanese: 彼女はそう言ってくれた。
lines.english: That was what she told me.

lines.japanese: 寂しくなると言ってくれた。
lines.english: She told me she would be lonely.

lines.japanese: 世界でただひとり、寂しくなると言ってくれた。
lines.english: She alone in all the world told me she would be lonely.

lines.japanese: 恋なんて知らないまま去ってゆくはずだった僕に、小さいけれどいつまでも塞がらない引っかき傷を入れていった。
lines.english: I had meant to depart without ever knowing love. Instead, she left me with a tiny scratch that would never quite close.

lines.japanese: だから──
lines.english: And so—

lines.japanese: ──いままた僕は携帯電話のメモ帳を開き、件名『残務処理』を呼びだしていた。
lines.english: —once again I opened the notes on my phone and called up the entry titled ‘Unfinished Business.’

lines.japanese: 忘れかけていた三大項目の下で、入力待ちのカーソルがせわしなく点滅している。
lines.english: Below the three major items I had nearly forgotten, the cursor blinked impatiently, waiting for me to type.

lines.japanese: それがあまりに鬱陶しくて気でも触れそうになったから、仕方なく僕は親指を動かした。
lines.english: It was so irritating I thought it might drive me mad. With little choice, I moved my thumb.

lines.japanese: “４：渡来さんと”
lines.english: ‘4. With Watarai…’

lines.japanese: しかしそこまで打って、はたと止まる。
lines.english: There I stopped short.

lines.japanese: にわかに顔が熱くなった。僕はいったい何を打とうとしてるんだろう。
lines.english: My face abruptly grew hot. What in the world had I been about to write?

lines.japanese: だいたいこんな実在する固有名詞を入れて、万が一誰かの目にでも触れたら大変なことになる。
lines.english: Besides, putting a real person’s actual name in here would be a disaster if anyone ever happened to see it.

lines.japanese: 僕はぷちぷちぷちとクリアボタンを連打して頭から入れなおした。
lines.english: I hit the clear key—click, click, click—erased it, and started over.

lines.japanese: “４：Ｗさんと”
lines.english: ‘4. With W…’

lines.japanese: やっぱり止まる。
lines.english: Again, I stopped.

lines.japanese: Ｗさんと……なんだっていうんだ？
lines.english: With W… what?

lines.japanese: “４：Ｗさんと仲良くなる”
lines.english: ‘4. Grow closer to W.’

lines.japanese: おそるおそる打ちこんでみたものの、どうにも漠然としている。
lines.english: I entered it timidly, but it was hopelessly vague.

lines.japanese: 仲良くなる……とは言っても、何をもって仲が良いとするんだろう。もっと具体的な目標を定めるべきなのか。
lines.english: Grow closer… What would qualify as close? Perhaps I needed a more concrete objective.

lines.japanese: “４：Ｗさんとキスす”
lines.english: ‘4. Give W a ki—’

lines.japanese: 最後まで打てなかった。
lines.english: I could not finish typing it.

lines.japanese: なんだろう、このムズ痒さは。高望みとかいう以前に、痛い。
lines.english: What was this squirmy feeling? Forget aiming too high. This was just painful.

lines.japanese: たぶんキスという言葉が悪いんだろう。歌詞や映画の中ならともかく、日本人の日常には溶けこみにくい単語だ。
lines.english: Maybe the word kiss was the problem. Fine in songs or movies, but it just wasn’t a word that fit into everyday life in Japan.

lines.japanese: それに妙な生々しさが拭えない。もっと冗談じみてるぐらいが適当だろう。
lines.english: And it still felt weirdly too real. Better to make it sound more like a joke.

lines.japanese: “４：Ｗさんと結婚する”
lines.english: ‘4. Marry W.’

lines.japanese: まさか。余命いくばくもないのに、それは大望が過ぎるってもんだ。
lines.english: No way. With barely any time left to live, that’d be asking for way too much.

lines.japanese: それに僕はそこまで身のほど知らずな人間じゃない。そんな大それたことを望んでるわけじゃなくて、もっとありふれた、せいぜいが──
lines.english: And I was not so ignorant of my own station. I wanted nothing so outrageous—only something more ordinary. At most—

lines.japanese: “４：Ｗさんとデートする”
lines.english: ‘4. Go on a date with W.’

lines.japanese: ──このぐらいだろう。
lines.english: —something like that.

lines.japanese: いや、でもなんか……まだやっぱり……。
lines.english: No. Even that still felt somehow… wrong.

lines.japanese: 分かった。デートって単語がおこがましいんだ。
lines.english: I understood. The word date was presumptuous.

lines.japanese: “４：Ｗさんと遊びに行く”
lines.english: ‘4. Go somewhere fun with W.’

lines.japanese: これだ。
lines.english: There.

lines.japanese: ほどよく分を弁えた目標に、僕はひとり頷いた。
lines.english: Alone, I nodded at this suitably modest ambition.

lines.japanese: 新たに築かれた生き甲斐が、くすんだ生活に張りを与えてくれる。といいな。
lines.english: This new reason for living lent a little purpose to my drab existence. Or so I hoped.

lines.japanese: 僕は自らを鼓舞するつもりで、ケータイの隠しフォルダに保存してある一枚の画像を呼びだした。
lines.english: To hearten myself, I opened an image stored in a hidden folder on my phone.

lines.japanese: 僕はそれを眺めて温かな気持ちになる。
lines.english: Looking at it filled me with warmth.

lines.japanese: 去年の体育祭のとき、美術部作の装飾アーチを撮るふりしてこっそり収めた渡来さんの姿。
lines.english: It was a picture of Watarai from last year’s sports festival, secretly captured while I pretended to photograph the decorative arch made by the art club.

lines.japanese: 表情がこちらを向いていないのは残念だけど、ひとと目を合わせるのが苦手な僕には、このぐらいが丁度いいのかもしれない。
lines.english: It was a shame I couldn’t see her face, but since I was bad at looking people in the eye, maybe this was just right.

lines.japanese: 一方的に見ているだけの方が、楽でいいんだ。
lines.english: It was easier just watching her without her looking back.

lines.japanese: そして僕は、画面のバックライトが消えてもしばらくそのまま、４５度の横顔に見入っていた。
lines.english: Even after the screen’s backlight went dark, I remained as I was for a while, gazing at her face in three-quarter profile.

lines.japanese: 写真の中の彼女はちょっと胸を反り気味にしている姿勢のせいで、白い生地がやけに盛りあがって見える。
lines.english: She held her chest slightly forward in the photograph, making the white cloth of her uniform appear especially full.

lines.japanese: しかし豊かな胸に反して体の線は異常なぐらい細くて、瑞々しい素足もしなやかで眩しかった。
lines.english: Yet beneath that generous bosom, the lines of her body were almost impossibly slender, and her youthful bare legs were supple and dazzling.

lines.japanese: まぶしいなあ。
lines.english: She was dazzling.

lines.japanese: 僕はまったく輝かない自分を嘲るように笑って、そっと携帯電話を閉じた。
lines.english: I laughed as though mocking my own complete lack of radiance, then gently closed the phone.

lines.japanese: 真冬の白い空を仰いで立ちあがれば、青春という災難がもたらす厄介な情動に身体の芯が疼いていた。
lines.english: I rose and looked up at the white midwinter sky. At the core of my body throbbed the troublesome passions brought on by that calamity called youth.

lines.japanese: そんな獣たらしく凝り固まってしまった男の一部分を、僕は激しく忌み、疎んじ、蔑んでいる。汚らわしいとさえ思っている。
lines.english: I loathe and shun and scorn the part of a man that can harden with such bestial insistence. I find it filthy.

lines.japanese: 最低だ。最低の屑だ。
lines.english: The worst. The lowest kind of scum.

lines.japanese: こんなにも清らかな想いさえ、しばしば下卑た本能で濾してしまう男なんて生き物は、さっさといなくなってしまえばいいんだ。
lines.english: Even the purest feeling is so often strained through base instinct. The creature called man ought to hurry up and disappear from the earth.

lines.japanese: それはそれとして今日は帰ったら自慰をしようと思った。
lines.english: That aside, I decided I would masturbate when I got home.

lines.japanese: 激白、童貞のすべて。
lines.english: Shocking Confession: A Virgin Tells All.
